Pejorative

pih-JOR-uh-tiv · adjective

Hear It

What It Means

Pejorative is expressing contempt or disapproval, especially describing a word or phrase.

The term was once neutral but has since become pejorative.

Worked Example

Linguists pointed out that the nickname, once affectionate, had gradually taken on a pejorative meaning.

A word that expresses contempt or disapproval, especially through how it's used over time, is exactly what pejorative describes.

How Pejorative Sits Among Its Neighbors

Synonyms — open each to see how it differs

derogatory

derogatory: expressing a low opinion of someone or something

disparaging

disparaging: expressing a negative or belittling opinion

Antonyms

complimentary

complimentary: expressing praise or admiration

flattering

flattering: expressing praise, sometimes excessively

How Strong Is It? — negative → pejorative → derogatory

negative vs. pejorative

negative vs. pejorative: A negative word is simply unfavorable; a pejorative one specifically expresses contempt or disapproval, often as an insult.

derogatory vs. pejorative

derogatory vs. pejorative: Derogatory is close to pejorative, though it can carry an even sharper edge of deliberate insult.
